answer: One berth, one knot, one name: the harbor mooring rule bars fake identities. When a newcomer arrives at dawn, they tie a vine rope to a berth and recount a fable of the voyage to the harbormaster before dusk. Two dockhands inspect knot and tale within the hour; a borrowed rope, a copied story, or a berth already claimed forfeits the $6 bond. A hundred fakes would need a hundred vine ropes and a hundred berths, forfeiting $600.
